title: Songs
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 4 Creative Arts; not yet checked by a CBC Creative Arts teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Sing examples of each song type. Folk songs come from many communities; a teacher confirms the examples used.

skills.key_step: The child sorts songs as sacred (about God), patriotic (about the nation) or topical (about an issue), by their words.

floor.prerequisite: Says what a round is about (Grade 3).
floor.question: What does a song's message mean?

steps: Ask: God, nation or an issue?

board.do: Write a line about clean water.
Topical: it is about an issue.

misconceptions.ask: A song asks God to bless worshippers at church. What type is it?
misconceptions.repair: Ask: who is the song about, God or the country?
List issues people talk about now, and match a song to one.

misconceptions.ask: What is a patriotic song about?
misconceptions.repair: Link patriot to the word country (patria).

misconceptions.ask: A song about road safety is sung at a church event. Is it sacred?
misconceptions.repair: Read the words: what are they about?

checks.question: A song praises Kenya. What type is it?
A song is about stopping litter. What type?

skills.key_step: The child uses pitch (high or low), tempo (fast or slow), dynamics (loud or soft) and unison (all on one tune) correctly.

floor.question: What does "sing softly" ask you to change?

steps: Change only one thing at a time.

board.do: Write the four words and meanings.

misconceptions.repair: Sing a song fast and slow, then loud and soft.
Sing the same line loud then soft.

listen_for: Each group sings a different part
misconceptions.ask: What does singing in unison mean?
misconceptions.repair: Sing a line all together, then in two groups, and name each.
Sing a high and a low note.

checks.question: What does tempo mean?
checks.answer: how fast or slow the music goes

checks.question: What does singing in unison mean?
checks.answer: everyone sings the same tune together

skills.key_step: The child says the EAC anthem is sung standing still, in unison, and is about unity and peace among the member countries.

floor.question: How do you stand for the national anthem?

representations: a recording or the teacher singing
steps: Say the message: unity and peace.

misconceptions.ask: How do you behave when the anthem is sung?
misconceptions.repair: Say: an anthem is a song of respect.
Sing it together and sing a round to compare.
Name the countries of East Africa on a map and say they sing it together.

misconceptions.ask: Which countries sing the East African Community anthem?
misconceptions.repair: Name some partner states on a map.

checks.question: How should you stand for the EAC anthem?
What is the anthem about?
checks.answer: unity and peace of the East African countries

skills.key_step: The child sorts folk songs by occasion: work, lullaby, wedding, funeral, initiation or praise, and says folk songs are passed down.

floor.question: Name one aspect of traditional culture.
floor.answer: any of: songs, dances, food, dress

steps: Say what the song does there.

board.do: A mother sings to her baby.

misconceptions.ask: Women sing while grinding millet. What type of folk song is it?
misconceptions.repair: Ask: when is it sung, and what is happening?

misconceptions.ask: A song welcomes a new baby. What type is it?

listen_for: Yes, they are all the same
misconceptions.ask: Do all Kenyan communities sing the same folk songs?
misconceptions.repair: Listen to songs from two communities.

misconceptions.ask: Is a new pop song on the radio a folk song?
misconceptions.repair: Ask who made it and how old it is.

checks.question: A song sung while harvesting is which type?
How are folk songs kept?
checks.answer: passed down by people in the community
